expert: Speed-typing expert (150+ WPM typist and layout analyst)
lens: WPM and accuracy on this user's real text (Rust snake_case, Vim and tmux commands, shell lines, fast chat), measured in same-finger bigrams, roll tolerance, tap-hold misfires and keystrokes per symbol.

support: Shift on a thumb and only ⌃⌥⌘ on the home row avoid the worst home-row-mod failure (Shift rolls in prose), and Chordal Hold makes every shortcut a cross-hand chord.
`:` on the pinky home turns `::` into two home-row taps, and Flow Tap keeps both as taps in flow because the Oryx placeholder taps as a letter.
⇧; → ? at the ANSI slash spot puts `?` where Mac hands expect it, at no extra keystrokes.
⇧⏎ as a single thumb tap is the cheapest possible newline, and it can never send a half-written message.
layers.verdict: Keep it as it is: the base is already fast, and the remaining speed gains are in the tap-hold settings, not the key positions.

support: Digits on the right under a left-thumb hold are opposite-hand, and the 789/456/123 grid is the numpad your hands already know.
Transparent `=` and Bspc mean `+=`, `-=`, `==` and digit fixes happen without lifting the thumb, and `/` at the ANSI spot keeps `//` comments on muscle memory.
Keeping 0 on N rather than on a thumb is right: on R-outer, a rolled single `0` (NUM thumb released first) would leak ⇧⏎ + Esc, which throws Vim out of insert mode.
R-inner should stay transparent even without the tri-layer, so that a NUM→SYM roll (`u8>`, `0]`, `1)`) reaches SYM, which outranks NUM.
Dropping the ⌘1/⌘2 tap dance removes a tap-dance timeout; ⌘ on D plus a digit is a plain chord.

changes.key: Numbers, left top Q and left bottom B
changes.why: `git checkout -b`, `0b1010` and `64bit` roll straight from a NUM key into B and would lock the layer, so everything typed after it becomes IDE commands. A q almost never follows a digit or `-`, and a stray ⌘. only opens the quick-fix menu.

layers.verdict: A fast numpad whose real risk is the thumb still being down when the next letter lands on the left-hand IDE keys, so pair it with the NUM guard in config.

support: Taking SYM off Space is the draft's biggest speed fix: Space keeps Flow Tap, and `_` or `(` mid-word no longer competes with the prose key.
With the thumb on the right, `( ) [ ] < > & ! #` are opposite-hand chords, the fastest layer geometry.
`->` and `=>` as one-chord macros save a keystroke each on Rust's two most common digraphs.
The transparent bottom right (`m , . ; =`) lets `);`, `),`, `).`, `!=`, `<=` and `)?;` flow with the thumb still down.

changes.key: Symbols, left home A ↔ right home H
changes.why: On the right index, `_` forms same-finger bigrams with n, m, u, y and j in about 30% of Rust snake_case joins (`get_mut`, `fn_name`, `try_into`, `is_none`). On the left pinky only q and z collide (under 1%), `_a` is a cheap same-key repeat, `_` becomes opposite-hand to the SYM thumb, `?` stays on the layer, and `)?;` is still one SYM hold.

changes.key: Symbols, right top O and P, right bottom N
changes.why: If the thumb is still down after `_`, a `--` swallows the next letter (`unwrap_or` → `unwrap_r`, `_ptr`, `_name`). Transparent keys let o, p and n through, and on a SYM→NUM overlap N falls through to NUM's 0, so `[0]` survives.

layers.verdict: The structure is right, and two small edits cut `_` same-finger bigrams sharply and make the layer tolerate a late thumb release.

support: Plain ⌃⌥⌘⇧ on the left home (no tap-hold) make ⌥⇧→ word-select and ⌘⇧← line-select instant once Space is held.
Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Redo on Z X C V B keep the Mac shapes, so editing bursts need no relearning.
Enter on R-inner next to the arrows lets you pick a menu item with `↓↓⏎` without releasing anything.
A lean layer suits a Space-held layer: fewer live keys means fewer surprises from a lingering Space.

changes.key: Nav, right top Y U I O (tmux)
changes.from: Right Option ⌥P/⌥H/⌥L/⌥N (RALT, as in the current keymap)
changes.why: Many macOS terminals keep Right Option for special characters, so ⌥H can type ˙ instead of reaching tmux. Left Option is the side terminals usually map to Meta.

layers.verdict: Good and lean; only the tmux modifier side needs fixing.

support: Expert A's block mirrors the numpad, so F5 sits where 5 is and F12 on the pinky top, with nothing new to learn.
Mods on the right home give one-hand ⇧F12 and ⌘+F-key chords without home-row-mod timing.
Boot and Lock in the far corners can't be reached by a roll.

changes.to: chord: L-inner + R-inner pressed within 35 ms → MO(F) (combo; C if Oryx can't output it)
changes.why: In Rust the inner thumbs overlap constantly (`[0]`, `(1, 2)`, `Vec<u8>`, `1_000`), and with a plain tri-layer the digits land on ⌘⇧4, RGB and Mute while brackets land on F2 (rename), F5 (start debugging) and F9 (breakpoint). A 35 ms press window only fires when you press both thumbs together on purpose.

layers.verdict: The content is right; change only how you reach it.

support: All four tap jobs suit speed: Space and Shift sit on the two resting thumbs, and each layer's content is on the opposite hand from its thumb.
A leaked NUM tap gives ⇧⏎, which in chat apps is only a newline, never a send.
Esc on a thumb is the fastest Esc a Vim user can have, and Shift on the same thumb keeps capitals off the pinky.
concerns: As specified, real Enter (hold Space + R-inner) only works if Space stays down past the 200 ms tapping term, so a quick chord comes out as space + Tab. It also needs a pause after the last letter, or Flow Tap forces a space: about 350 ms per send or shell command.
The plain NUM+SYM tri-layer turns common Rust rolls into F-key and media misfires (see F-keys).

Esc/⇧ is the touchiest key: with permissive hold, a capital whose thumb lifts before the letter becomes Esc + lowercase, which runs commands in Vim insert mode. Hold the thumb through the letter, or use OS⇧ when unsure.
Optional: if you ever relax 'real Enter only on a layer', tapping the same inner-thumb chord could send Enter in one motion, and a single thumb tap still couldn't send.

config: `TAPPING_TERM 200` with `TAPPING_TERM_PER_KEY`: 160 ms for Esc/⇧, so a lingering capital roll resolves as Shift (real Esc taps last under 100 ms), and 200 ms for everything else.

`PERMISSIVE_HOLD_PER_KEY`: on for A S D K L :, ⇧⏎/NUM, Tab/SYM and Esc/⇧. Don't copy Expert B's `false` for Esc/⇧: with it off, any capital typed in under 200 ms comes out as Esc + lowercase (the QMK docs' 'ax' case).

Space/NAV: permissive hold off, except when the nested key is R-inner (C: in `pre_process_record_user`, which runs before tap-hold buffering, record whether the last press was `LT(SYM, KC_TAB)`, then return that flag from `get_permissive_hold` for the Space key). Enter then fires when R-inner is released, and letters inside a lingering Space still type as spaces.

`HOLD_ON_OTHER_KEY_PRESS_PER_KEY`: true only for Tab/SYM, so a rolled symbol never leaks a Tab; Tab is rarely overlapped because you pause to read the completion. Never set it for NUM, where an in-flow newline overlap would fire IDE keys.
`CHORDAL_HOLD` with all four thumbs set to '*' in `chordal_hold_layout`; otherwise right-hand capitals typed with the right Shift thumb (I, You, Ok) are forced to Esc.

Write `get_flow_tap_term` explicitly: 150 ms for A S D K L :, 120 ms for Space/NAV (permissive hold off already guards in-flow spaces, and a shorter window lets Enter or ⌥← follow typing sooner), and 0 for NUM, SYM and Esc/⇧. The default would treat Oryx's DUAL_FUNC placeholder for ⇧⏎/NUM (an LT with a letter tap) as a letter and force newlines into `u8` or `i32`.
`QUICK_TAP_TERM 120` on the home-row mods (keeps `kkkk` repeat in Vim), and 0 on every thumb, so ⇧⏎ followed quickly by a NUM hold gives `2.` for a chat list instead of auto-repeated newlines.

`COMBO_TERM 35` for the inner-thumb F chord. Add a NUM guard (C): a left-hand NUM key pressed within 150 ms of a right-hand NUM key turns NUM off and sends its base letter, so `-r`, `3rd` or `0x` can't fire IDE commands.
warnings: Single-digit rolls (`u8`, `[0]`, `x2`) still leak a NUM tap if the thumb lifts first. In chat that's a stray newline, but in a default macOS terminal ⇧⏎ is CR, so it runs the half-typed command.

Without the NUM guard, a late thumb release fires IDE keys mid-word: `-r`/`3rd` → ⌘⇧H, `-t`/`4th` → terminal toggle, `-f` → ⌘⇧F, `-v` → ⌥Space, and `0x`/`-x` silently overwrite the clipboard with a file path.
`/` on NUM sits on the base `;` key, so `let n = 42;` with the thumb still down types `42/`. That's the price of keeping `//` at the ANSI spot.
`-` lives only on NUM, so hyphenated words, `- ` chat bullets and CLI flags are all layer chords and roll hazards.
Zero on N shares the index finger with 1, 4, 7, + and -, so `10`, `100`, `40` and `70` are same-finger bigrams; accept it, because a thumb zero leaks Esc on rolls.
`=` on the bottom outer pinky is the slowest base spot for one of Rust's most frequent symbols; Expert B's base fixes it there, so it's a ceiling, not a bug.
In VS Code, ⇧⏎ with the suggest widget open accepts the alternative suggestion instead of inserting a newline, and in find bars it jumps to the previous match.
The `_`/`?` swap is the one change that touches years of muscle memory; expect a week or two of slower snake_case before it pays off.
